match.reason: No single bank point teaches this idea: the relationship marketing card is close but also covers societal marketing, and the customer service card covers complaints but not loyalty or the lower cost of keeping customers, so a new point is the safer choice.

draft.title: Customer relationships
card: A customer relationship is the ongoing connection between a business and the people who buy from it. Businesses build it so customers come back.
Good service, loyalty programs and handling complaints well are three ways to keep customers. A loyalty program rewards repeat buying, for example with points or discounts.
Keeping an existing customer usually costs less than winning a new one, because finding new customers needs advertising and special offers.
A complaint dealt with quickly and fairly gives the business a chance to keep the customer. It also shows the business where its service falls short.
draft.remember: Keeping a customer usually costs less than finding a new one.

a.q: Why do businesses put effort into keeping existing customers?
opts: It usually costs less than finding new customers
It removes the need to handle any complaints
It means the business no longer needs to advertise
It guarantees that customers will never leave
a.why: Winning new customers needs advertising and offers, so keeping current ones usually costs less. Good relationships do not remove complaints or advertising, and they cannot guarantee that customers stay.
a.clue: Think about what it costs to find someone new.

b.q: Priya owns a bike repair shop in Ballarat. A customer complains that a repair took a week longer than promised. What should Priya do to best protect the relationship?
opts: Apologise, fix the problem and offer a small discount
Explain that delays are normal and make no changes
Ask the customer to leave a review before anything else
Spend the money on advertising to find new customers
b.why: Dealing with the complaint quickly and fairly gives Priya the best chance of keeping the customer. Advertising for new customers costs more, and ignoring the complaint risks losing the customer.
b.clue: A complaint is a chance to keep the customer.

a.best: It usually costs less than finding new customers

b.best: Apologise, fix the problem and offer a small discount

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with a hedge ('usually'). Every distractor is an absolute ('any', 'no longer', 'guarantees', 'never'), so a student could pick the answer by spotting the absolutes without knowing the idea.
The clue 'Think about what it costs to find someone new' points straight at the only option that mentions cost, which gives the answer away.

a.q: A café owner is weighing up keeping regulars against winning new customers. How do the costs usually compare?
opts: Keeping regulars costs less, as less advertising is needed
Keeping regulars costs more, as loyalty rewards are dear
Both cost about the same, as both need special offers
Keeping regulars costs more, as complaints take staff time
a.why: New customers have to be found through advertising and special offers, so keeping existing ones usually costs less. Loyalty rewards and complaint handling do cost something, but not more than the effort of winning someone new.
a.clue: Who already knows the café, and who does not?
